# Stakeholder Communication Matrix

## Purpose
Define communication channels, frequency, and responsibilities for keeping stakeholders informed and engaged throughout the project lifecycle.

---

## Communication Principles
- **Transparency**: Share progress, risks, and decisions openly
- **Timeliness**: Communicate at regular intervals and when significant changes occur
- **Relevance**: Tailor content to stakeholder needs and interests
- **Two-way**: Encourage feedback and questions from stakeholders

---

## Stakeholder Groups

### Executive Sponsors
**Who**: C-level executives, VPs sponsoring the initiative  
**Interest Level**: High-level outcomes, ROI, strategic alignment  
**Communication Needs**: Business impact, major milestones, budget/timeline risks

| Communication Type | Frequency | Owner | Format | Participants |
|-------------------|-----------|-------|--------|--------------|
| Sponsor briefing | Monthly or at milestones | PM | Presentation + Q&A | PM, Product Manager, Sponsor |
| Major decision requests | As needed | PM with Product Owner | Email or meeting | PM, Product Owner, Product Manager, Sponsor |
| Critical escalations | Immediate | PM | Email + meeting | PM, Product Manager, Sponsor |

---

### Product Leadership
**Who**: Product VPs, Directors overseeing product strategy  
**Interest Level**: Product outcomes, user impact, roadmap alignment  
**Communication Needs**: Feature progress, user feedback, prioritization decisions

| Communication Type | Frequency | Owner | Format | Participants |
|-------------------|-----------|-------|--------|--------------|
| Product sync | Weekly | Product Manager | Meeting | Product Manager, Product Owner, PM |
| Roadmap updates | Monthly | Product Manager | Document + review | Product Manager, Product Owner, PM, UX/UI Designer |
| User research findings | As completed | UX/UI Designer | Presentation | UX/UI Designer, Product Owner, Product Manager |
| Feature demos | End of sprint/milestone | Product Owner | Demo session | Product Owner, Developers, Product Manager, Stakeholders |

---

### Engineering Leadership
**Who**: Engineering VPs, Directors, Architects  
**Interest Level**: Technical approach, architecture, quality, resource needs  
**Communication Needs**: Technical decisions, risks, dependencies, staffing

| Communication Type | Frequency | Owner | Format | Participants |
|-------------------|-----------|-------|--------|--------------|
| Engineering sync | Bi-weekly | PM | Meeting | PM, Scrum Master, Tech Lead, DevOps Engineer, Eng Leadership |
| Technical design reviews | As needed | Tech Lead/Developers | Document + meeting | Developers, DevOps Engineer, QA Lead, Eng Leadership |
| Infrastructure updates | Monthly | DevOps Engineer | Email or meeting | DevOps Engineer, PM, Eng Leadership |
| Quality metrics review | Monthly | QA Lead | Dashboard + summary | QA Lead, PM, Eng Leadership |

---

### Cross-functional Teams
**Who**: Marketing, Sales, Support, Operations teams  
**Interest Level**: Feature readiness, launch timelines, training needs  
**Communication Needs**: Release dates, new capabilities, customer impact

| Communication Type | Frequency | Owner | Format | Participants |
|-------------------|-----------|-------|--------|--------------|
| Release readiness | 2 weeks before release | PM | Meeting | PM, Product Owner, Marketing, Sales, Support |
| Release notes | At each release | PM | Document | PM with input from Product Owner, Developers |
| Feature training | Before major releases | Product Owner | Training session | Product Owner, UX/UI Designer, Support, Sales |
| Go-to-market planning | 4-6 weeks before launch | Product Manager | Planning sessions | Product Manager, Product Owner, Marketing, Sales |

---

### Development Team
**Who**: All team members building and delivering the product  
**Interest Level**: Day-to-day execution, blockers, clarity on requirements  
**Communication Needs**: Task details, priorities, feedback, support

| Communication Type | Frequency | Owner | Format | Participants |
|-------------------|-----------|-------|--------|--------------|
| Daily standup | Daily (15 min) | Scrum Master | Standup meeting | All team members |
| Sprint planning | Start of sprint | Scrum Master | Meeting | Product Owner, Scrum Master, Developers, UX/UI Designer, QA Lead, DevOps Engineer |
| Backlog refinement | Weekly or bi-weekly | Product Owner | Meeting | Product Owner, Developers, QA Lead, UX/UI Designer |
| Sprint review/demo | End of sprint | Scrum Master | Demo session | All team + invited stakeholders |
| Sprint retrospective | End of sprint | Scrum Master | Facilitated discussion | All team members |
| Design reviews | As needed | UX/UI Designer | Review session | UX/UI Designer, Product Owner, Developers |

---

### End Users / Customers
**Who**: People who use the product  
**Interest Level**: New features, improvements, bug fixes  
**Communication Needs**: Product updates, how to use new features, support

| Communication Type | Frequency | Owner | Format | Participants |
|-------------------|-----------|-------|--------|--------------|
| Product updates | Monthly or at releases | Product Manager | Blog post, email | Product Manager, Product Owner |
| Feature announcements | At major releases | Product Manager | Email, in-app notification | Product Manager with PM input |
| User research sessions | Ongoing | UX/UI Designer | Interviews, surveys, usability tests | UX/UI Designer, Product Owner |
| Beta programs | For major features | Product Owner | Closed beta + feedback loop | Product Owner, UX/UI Designer, selected users |

---

## Communication Templates

### Weekly Status Update Template
**To**: Product Leadership, Engineering Leadership  
**From**: PM  
**Frequency**: Weekly

**Progress this week:**
- [Completed items]

**Next week's goals:**
- [Planned items]

**Risks & blockers:**
- [Current risks with mitigation plans]

**Decisions needed:**
- [Any pending decisions with deadline]

---

### Sprint Review Summary Template
**To**: Stakeholders, Product Leadership  
**From**: Product Owner  
**Frequency**: End of sprint

**Sprint goals:** [What we planned]  
**Completed:** [What we delivered]  
**Demo highlights:** [Link to demo or screenshots]  
**Upcoming:** [Next sprint focus]  
**Feedback requested:** [Specific questions or areas for input]

---

### Release Communication Template
**To**: Cross-functional teams, End Users  
**From**: PM  
**Frequency**: At each release

**Release:** [Version/Name]  
**Date:** [Release date]  
**What's new:**
- [Feature 1]
- [Feature 2]

**Improvements:**
- [Enhancement 1]

**Bug fixes:**
- [Fix 1]

**Documentation:** [Link to user guide or help docs]  
**Feedback:** [How to provide feedback]

---

## Escalation Communication

When escalating issues, use the following structure:

**Subject**: [Clear, specific subject line]

**Situation**: [Brief context]  
**Impact**: [Business or customer impact]  
**Proposed action**: [Recommended next steps]  
**Decision needed by**: [Deadline with rationale]  
**Owner**: [Who will execute the decision]

---

## Tips for Effective Stakeholder Communication

1. **Know your audience**: Tailor content to their level and interests
2. **Lead with impact**: Start with outcomes and business value
3. **Be concise**: Respect stakeholders' time with clear, brief updates
4. **Use visuals**: Dashboards, charts, and demos are more engaging than text
5. **Invite feedback**: Make it easy for stakeholders to ask questions and provide input
6. **Be proactive**: Share risks and issues early, with mitigation plans
7. **Follow up**: Document decisions and action items from meetings
